subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: Should macOS app-backed nodes be probed immediately on connect, probed only after a stronger readiness/deferred backoff signal, or skipped only when co-located with the gateway?
rationale: Current main now supports macOS `system.which` and `system.run`, but the remaining behavior crosses readiness timing, co-location detection, retry/backoff policy, and the node exec contract.

options.title: Narrow Active-Runtime Fix
options.body: Keep the app-node exec contract intact, implement the probe timing or co-location rule in `src/skills/runtime/remote.ts`, and require real macOS proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Skip Only Co-located App Nodes
options.body: Avoid probing loopback/co-located app nodes while preserving remote app-node probing for hosts that can execute skills.

options.title: Disable App-node Probing By Default
options.body: Stop automatic app-node remote skill eligibility unless users explicitly enable it, reducing warning spam at the cost of default remote skill support.

recommendation.title: Narrow Active-Runtime Fix
recommendation.body: Keep the app-node exec contract intact, implement the probe timing or co-location rule in `src/skills/runtime/remote.ts`, and require real macOS proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The remote skill probe and node command-policy history makes this the best available routing owner for the product boundary choice.
